items.title: NVIDIA Is Buying a Piece of Meta: What the $3 Billion Stake Means
items.summary: The company that sells Meta its AI chips is now buying a piece of Meta itself. NVIDIA is putting $3 billion into Meta's stock offering, making Jensen Huang's chip giant a shareholder in one of its biggest customers. In this video, Eric Bleeker, CFA, Chief Investment Officer of 24/7 Wall St., examines why Meta Platforms (NASDAQ: META) is raising as much as $95 billion, and what NVIDIA (NASDAQ: NVDA) gets beyond the shares. With Meta guiding to as much as $145 billion in capital spending and posting negative free cash flow, the biggest questions are whether this is smart partnership or circular financing, and how much dilution Meta shareholders should expect. We'll also look at Muse, Meta's personal AI agent, which signed up more than 10 million users in about six weeks and could drive years of demand for NVIDIA hardware. Finally, we'll discuss the two numbers that will decide whether this spending pays off: Meta's AI revenue starting in 2027, and Zuckerberg's goal of making Muse more than 10 times cheaper to run.

analysis.summary: NVIDIA is investing $3 billion to buy shares in Meta’s secondary offering, turning its biggest AI‑chip customer into a fellow shareholder.
analysis.catalyst: NVIDIA’s $3 bn stake purchase in Meta’s stock offering
analysis.horizon: 3‑6 months, until the next earnings season or any material update on the Nvidia‑Meta partnership
analysis.explanation: NVIDIA just committed $3 bn to buy Meta stock, signalling deep confidence in Meta’s AI roadmap and cementing the relationship with its biggest AI‑chip customer. That capital allocation shows Nvidia has excess cash and believes the partnership will drive higher demand for its GPUs, especially as Meta rolls out new AI features. Over the next few months, we expect Meta’s AI initiatives to boost Nvidia’s order backlog, supporting revenue growth and potentially lifting the stock ahead of its next earnings. The market’s neutral sentiment is outweighed by the strategic upside, making a long position in Nvidia the most direct way to capture the upside. Alternatives like buying Meta would be more speculative on the social‑media side, whereas Nvidia directly benefits from the AI spend acceleration.
rationale: Strategic cash deployment signals confidence in AI partnership with Meta
Boosts Nvidia’s growth outlook as Meta ramps AI services
Long NVDA captures upside without exposure to Meta’s broader business risk
analysis.risk: If Meta’s AI rollout stalls or the broader AI spending cycle slows, the expected boost to Nvidia’s revenue may not materialize, pressuring the stock.

items.title: Nvidia's Credit Risk Has Tripled This Year — and Just Passed Meta's
items.summary: Anyone who has co-signed a loan for a friend knows how the story can end. When the payments stop, the bank calls you. Nvidia Corp. (NASDAQ:NVDA) has co-signed a lot of loans. It owns a stake in CoreWeave Inc. (NASDAQ:CRWV). It has promised to buy computing capacity the neocloud cannot sell. It also guarantees part of the data center leases signed by its AI cloud partners. Now credit traders are pricing the phone call. The cost of protecting against an Nvidia default has more than tripled this ye

analysis.summary: Nvidia's five‑year credit default swap spread has more than tripled this year, now exceeding that of major customer Meta, as the chipmaker’s guarantees on AI‑cloud partner CoreWeave raise concerns about its credit quality.
analysis.catalyst: Rapid widening of Nvidia's CDS spread after its $2 billion stake and guarantee commitments to CoreWeave
analysis.horizon: 2‑4 weeks, or until the CDS spread stabilises below 100 bps or Nvidia issues a clear credit‑risk mitigation update
analysis.explanation: Nvidia has taken on significant contingent liabilities by co‑signing loans and guaranteeing data‑center leases for CoreWeave and other AI partners. This exposure has pushed its five‑year CDS spread to 127 bps, up 226% year‑to‑date, now higher than Meta’s. A widening CDS signals rising perceived default risk, which typically drags equity prices as investors demand a higher risk premium. The neutral sentiment from the article suggests no immediate positive news to offset the credit concerns. By shorting NVDA we capture the downside risk while the market digests the credit‑risk narrative; a longer‑dated put or a short‑term equity position aligns with the swing‑trade horizon. Alternative trades like buying the CDS directly are less accessible for a student fund, making the equity short the most practical expression of the thesis.
rationale: Nvidia’s CDS spread has exploded, indicating higher default risk
Equity prices tend to fall as credit risk perception rises
Short position captures downside over a 2‑4 week window as credit concerns play out
analysis.risk: If Nvidia’s AI revenue accelerates faster than expected or it announces a strong balance‑sheet recap, the credit spread could compress, lifting the stock and hurting the short.

analysis.explanation: Amazon’s shares have rallied 9.9% over the past three months but slipped 5.2% this week, creating a sharp contrast between momentum and recent weakness. Analysts estimate a fair value of $475 versus the current $249 price, implying roughly a 48% discount. The earnings call will reveal whether AWS AI capex is translating into higher margins and whether retail profitability is stabilising, which are the two key drivers of that valuation gap. A beat or strong guidance would likely close the discount as investors re‑price the high‑margin cloud and advertising engines, making a long position attractive. The negative sentiment from the NLP model reflects short‑term uncertainty, but the fundamental undervaluation and earnings catalyst support a swing‑trade long stance rather than a short‑term speculative play.
rationale: ~48% valuation gap suggests upside if earnings beat expectations
AWS AI spend is the primary growth engine; earnings will confirm its traction
Retail side risk is limited to short‑term margin pressure, not core valuation
analysis.risk: If AWS AI demand or retail margins fall short of expectations, the valuation gap could widen and the stock may stay depressed through the earnings window.

items.title: Up 16% This Year, How Long Can Procter & Gamble Continue Outperforming the S&P 500?
items.summary: Procter & Gamble is topping the broader market this year, but it may be part of a cautionary tale.

analysis.summary: Procter & Gamble (PG) has outperformed the S&P 500 by about 320 basis points YTD, buoyed by a defensive rotation away from AI‑heavy tech stocks, but the consumer‑staples sector now trades at a rich valuation relative to tech.
analysis.catalyst: Recent sector rotation into defensive consumer‑staples amid AI‑related market uncertainty
analysis.horizon: 3-5 months, until the AI‑driven risk premium eases or the sector P/E narrows relative to the broader market
analysis.explanation: PG is a Dividend King with a 2.7% yield and a YTD gain of 15.6%, well above the S&P 500. The market’s current fear of AI‑related volatility is pushing investors toward defensive names, giving PG a tailwind. While the consumer‑staples index now trades at a higher P/E than tech, the premium is justified by the safety premium and strong cash flow that supports dividend growth. Over the next few months, if the rotation persists, PG should continue to beat the market, and its dividend yield remains attractive versus Treasuries. A long equity position captures both price appreciation and dividend income, whereas alternatives like ETFs would dilute the specific upside of PG’s earnings momentum.
rationale: Defensive rotation supports price upside
Strong dividend yield adds income buffer
YTD outperformance signals momentum
analysis.risk: If AI‑related concerns fade quickly and investors swing back to growth stocks, the defensive premium could evaporate and PG may underperform.

analysis.summary: Wall Street analysts issued a series of upgrades and downgrades on Tuesday, including a positive upgrade for Occidental Petroleum (OXY) amid easing oil prices and potential geopolitical de‑escalation.
analysis.catalyst: Analyst upgrade to OXY with a higher price target as oil prices stabilize and geopolitical risk recedes
analysis.horizon: 2-4 weeks, until the upgraded price target is reflected in the stock price or new earnings guidance is released
analysis.explanation: Analysts have raised their outlook on Occidental Petroleum, citing the recent dip in Brent and WTI prices and the prospect of reduced supply risk from Iran and Ukraine talks. Lower crude prices improve OXY's cash flow and margin outlook, while the upgrade signals that the market may have over‑reacted to recent price swings. Over the next few weeks, the stock should benefit from the sentiment shift and from any further price stabilization, making a long position attractive. The positive FinBERT sentiment reinforces the bullish narrative, and OXY's valuation remains reasonable relative to peers, offering upside potential if the upgrade is fully priced in. We choose the equity itself rather than an oil ETF because the catalyst is company‑specific and the upgrade directly targets OXY's share price.
rationale: Analyst upgrade lifts price target, indicating upside
Oil price pull‑back improves OXY margins
Positive sentiment and lower geopolitical risk support rally
analysis.risk: If oil prices fall sharply again or the geopolitical situation worsens, OXY's earnings could be hit and the upgrade may be rescinded.

items.title: Mosaic (MOS) Stock Looks Undervalued Against the Sales It Generates
items.summary: Mosaic has seen its share price fall over several years, even though investors still look at it as a key fertilizer producer tied closely to global crop demand. With the stock now around US$18.79, the live issue is whether that market value can be sensibly explained by the company’s sales. Over the past 5 years, Mosaic’s share price has fallen 43.4%, which puts added focus on whether today’s valuation lines up with the revenue the business is generating. analysis.summary: Mosaic (MOS) is trading at a price‑to‑sales multiple of about 0.5x, well below the chemicals industry average and its peer group, suggesting the stock may be undervalued relative to its revenue generation.
analysis.catalyst: Analyst‑driven sales‑multiple valuation gap indicating Mosaic is trading below its fair P/S benchmark
analysis.horizon: 3-6 months, until the market re‑prices the stock toward its sector‑adjusted fair P/S multiple or a earnings update confirms margin improvement
analysis.explanation: Mosaic’s share price has fallen 43% over five years, yet its price‑to‑sales ratio remains roughly half of the industry norm. That discrepancy signals a valuation mismatch that can correct as investors recognize the low multiple. The fertilizer sector is cyclical, but the current low multiple provides a margin of safety, especially given Mosaic’s cash‑flow generation and potential upside from reallocating capital to higher‑margin projects like Mosaic Biosciences. Over the next few months, any positive earnings guidance or evidence of margin expansion should push the stock toward its fair‑value multiple, delivering upside. A long position captures that re‑rating while the negative sentiment is outweighed by the quantitative valuation gap.
rationale: P/S ~0.5x vs industry ~1.0x – clear discount
Strong cash flow and potential high‑margin project upside
Valuation gap offers upside if market re‑prices the stock
analysis.risk: If fertilizer demand weakens sharply or Mosaic’s cost structure deteriorates, the low multiple could reflect genuine risk, keeping the stock depressed.

items.title: $10,000 Invested in Eli Lilly 5 Years Ago Would Be Worth This Much Today
items.summary: The company has made longtime shareholders much richer.

analysis.summary: Eli Lilly’s stock has delivered a 40% annualized return over the past five years, far outpacing the S&P 500, and analysts cite its leadership in GLP‑1 drugs and deep pipeline as reasons to expect continued outperformance.
analysis.catalyst: Analyst commentary highlighting Lilly’s dominant GLP‑1 position and robust pipeline as a catalyst for sustained earnings growth through 2031
analysis.horizon: 6-12 months, until the next earnings season or a material pipeline update (e.g., FDA approval of a GLP‑1 or other late‑stage drug)
analysis.explanation: Lilly has just posted a historic performance track record, driven by its GLP‑1 franchise and a pipeline that’s second to none in the pharma space. That growth story is still unfolding, with several late‑stage candidates expected to file for approval in the next 12‑18 months, which should keep revenue expanding and margins strong. The stock trades at a forward P/E that, while higher than the sector average, is justified by the higher growth trajectory and the premium investors are willing to pay for a company that can sustain 30‑plus percent earnings growth. With a positive sentiment signal and no immediate macro headwinds, a long position in LLY captures upside from both earnings beat expectations and potential FDA approvals. The trade horizon allows time for the next earnings report and any pipeline news to materialize, giving us a clear exit trigger if the stock underperforms expectations.
rationale: Strong historical returns and market‑leading GLP‑1 sales
Deep, diversified pipeline with multiple late‑stage candidates
Forward earnings growth outlook remains well above sector average
analysis.risk: A setback in GLP‑1 competition or a negative FDA decision on a late‑stage drug could stall earnings growth and depress the stock.
